# atlaspm

<!-- badges: start -->

[![check-prod](https://github.com/andredot/atlaspm/actions/workflows/check-prod.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/andredot/atlaspm/actions/workflows/check-prod.yaml)

**A Bayesian spatial analysis of avoidable mortality determinants in the
ATS Milano territory.**

`atlaspm` is the analysis code for an MPH Project at the London School
of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine estimating where avoidable deaths
cluster across the ATS Città Metropolitana di Milano territory, and how
much of that clustering is explained by area deprivation, air pollution
and primary care capacity.

It is an R package wrapped around a
[`targets`](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/) pipeline: the package
holds the functions, the pipeline holds the analysis, and a Quarto
document renders every reported number straight from the pipeline, so
nothing in the write-up is transcribed by hand.

> ### Status: active research code
>
> This is a thesis in progress. Findings are provisional and under
> revision; please don't cite numbers from this repository. The pipeline
> runs end to end on the real extracts the synthetic primary-care
> placeholder that stood in for the GP registry has been replaced by the
> 2023 care-burden-weighted indicator.

## What it estimates

An ecological analysis of **deaths before age 75 in 2022–2024**,
classified as avoidable using the joint OECD/Eurostat list, across **279
areal units**: 193 municipalities, less Milan, plus the 87 populated
Local Identity Units (NIL) into which Milan is disaggregated.

Three objectives:

1.  **Describe** the spatial distribution of avoidable mortality,
    estimating a smoothed risk surface that separates signal from
    small-count noise.
2.  **Explain** how much of the between-area variation is attributable
    to deprivation, air pollution and primary care supply — and report
    honestly how much is not.
3.  **Probe** one mechanism in depth, using time-to-treatment for stroke
    as a tracer condition with a negative control outcome.

The primary estimand is the **residual excess**: deaths occurring beyond
what an area's age and sex structure and measured covariates jointly
predict, i.e. relative to `E · exp(α + xβ)`, with the spatial random
effects deliberately excluded — including them would make the estimand
identically zero.

## Methods in brief

| Component | Approach |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Outcome | Deaths 0 to 74, 2022-2024, OECD/Eurostat avoidable list; fractional weights for causes split across the preventable and treatable lists |
| Denominator | Person-years summed over 2022-2024, so every rate is annualised |
| Standardisation | Indirect, internal standard, by single year of age and sex |
| Spatial model | BYM2 via `geostan::stan_icar()`, ICAR component scaled per Riebler et al. (2016) |
| Alternative | Eigenvector spatial filtering (`geostan::stan_esf()`), as a check on how the covariate/random-effect partition is drawn |
| Deprivation | Permanent-census reformulation of the Italian Deprivation Index (Rosano et al. 2020), built at areal-unit resolution against a national municipal reference distribution. Stability checked against the same four indicators computed from the 2011 general census |
| Primary care | Burden-adjusted GP supply: GP-equivalents per registered patient, each patient weighted by the national age-sex care-burden schedule. The unweighted predecessor is carried alongside, but it's not used |
| Air pollution | EEA 1 km interpolated concentration maps, area-weighted extraction |
| Stroke access | Population-weighted census-section origins, OSM road network, AREU emergency speed model, routed with `dodgr`. The routing is computed once and read back from a saved table |
| Exceedance | P(RR \> 1.10) \> 0.80 |

### The seven models

All share one Poisson likelihood with `log(expected)` as an offset,
which is what makes the leave-one-out comparison across them legitimate.

| ID  | Specification                         | Engine |
|-----|---------------------------------------|--------|
| M1  | Intercept only                        | GLM    |
| M2  | Covariates, no random effect          | GLM    |
| M3  | BYM2, no covariates                   | BYM2   |
| M4  | BYM2 + deprivation                    | BYM2   |
| M5  | BYM2 + deprivation, NO₂, primary care | BYM2   |
| M6  | As M5, eigenvector spatial filtering  | ESF    |
| M7  | As M5, PM2.5 in place of NO₂          | BYM2   |

Models are defined in a single `model_specs` tibble in `_targets.R` and
expanded by `tarchetypes::tar_map()`, so a formula is edited in exactly
one place and the target name, the table row and the figure panel all
follow. The same four-way structure — no spatial term, spatial term
alone, spatial term plus exposure, and an alternative spatial
parameterisation — is reused for the stroke sub-model, because a null
coefficient means something different in each and the four together
separate "no association" from "not identified".

## Data availability

**The individual-level mortality data cannot be shared.** Death records
come from the Lombardy Registro Nominativo delle Cause di Morte (ReNCaM)
under a data-sharing agreement with ATS Città Metropolitana di Milano,
and are held on a restricted network share.

The primary-care indicator is also restricted: it is an area-level
collapse of the regional assistance register (NAR), supplied as
`indicatore_assistenza_2023.csv`.

Everything else is public: ISTAT population, census and boundary
releases (including the 2011 general census at section level, used for
the deprivation stability check), EEA air quality maps, OpenStreetMap,
and the regional register of accredited stroke centres. The
avoidable-cause lookup (`avoidable_lookup_v3.csv`) is in the repository
and Appendix B of the report is generated from it, so the classification
as actually applied is fully inspectable even without the deaths.

Input paths resolve through two environment variables:

``` r
# .Renviron
PRJ_SHARED_PATH   = "/path/to/restricted/share"
INPUT_DATA_FOLDER = "input_data"
```

## Running it

``` r
# 1. restore the pinned dependency versions
renv::restore()

# 2. inspect the dependency graph before committing to a run
targets::tar_visnetwork(targets_only = TRUE)

# 3. run
.run()
```

One warning about cost: fitting seven models, seven per-mechanism
strata, the tracer and control panel and the all-age stroke outcomes is
a few hours on four cores.

The road-network build used to dominate that (10–40 minutes and 8-16
GB), and it needs an OSM extract on disk. Nothing downstream of
`stroke_times` touches the network object, so the routing is now
computed once and read back, at least for ATS Milan area:

``` r
# in _targets.R
tar_target(stroke_times_path, get_input_data_path("stroke_times.rds"),
           format = "file"),
tar_target(stroke_times, import_stroke_times(stroke_times_path,
                                             areas = area_shp$area)),
```

`format = "file"` means `targets` tracks the saved table by hash, so
replacing it rebuilds everything downstream. The routing functions are
unchanged and still tested; only the pipeline's entry point moved. To
re-run them (after a change to the centre list, the speed model or the
section origins) uncomment the block above them in `_targets.R` and save
the result back:

``` r
saveRDS(targets::tar_read(stroke_times),
        file.path(Sys.getenv("PRJ_SHARED_PATH"),
                  Sys.getenv("INPUT_DATA_FOLDER"), "stroke_times.rds"))
```

## Output

Two Quarto reports, both rendering to self-contained HTML with figures
written to `output/figures/` at 300 dpi.

**`reports/thesis_results.qmd`**: the main result tables and figures.
Opens with a numbers card listing every scalar the Results prose
interpolates, then works through descriptive epidemiology, covariate
distributions, model comparison, the risk surface and residual excess,
the seven mechanism strata, and the tracer and control panel.

**`reports/stroke_results.qmd`**: objective 3 subanalysis in depth. The
stroke network and its geocoding, travel-time surfaces, whether the
design has the exposure contrast to detect anything at all, the
outcome-definition problem (only a minority of premature cerebrovascular
deaths are the ischaemic strokes thrombectomy acts on), and the same set
of specifications applied to both the 0–74 avoidable outcome and the
all-age register outcomes.

Both regenerate from the pipeline, so no reported number is transcribed
by hand. Two exploratory scripts sit alongside them
(`explore_gp_supply.R` and `explore.R` ) which read targets and never
re-derive anything.

## Repository layout

```         
R/                    package functions
  import_.R           readers for each source
  preprocess_.R       cause classification, standardisation, person-years
  deprivation.R       Italian Deprivation Index at areal-unit resolution
  deprivation_2011.R  2011 census import and the stability check
  pollution_.R        EEA raster extraction and pollutant selection
  stroke.R            road network, routing, accessibility, saved-routing import
  stroke_report.R     stroke reporting: centre table, exposure contrast, maps
  nar_density.R       primary care supply from the register (upstream helpers)
  fit_model.R         one dispatcher for M1-M7
  model.R             BYM2 fitting, diagnostics, LOO comparison
  estimand.R          residual excess, variance decomposition, Moran's I
  controls.R          tracer and negative/positive controls
  describe.R          Table 1, flow counts, reported scalars
  summarise.R         fits -> tidy tables
  plot_.R             maps
  plot_report.R       publication figures
_targets.R            the pipeline
reports/              two Quarto reports + exploratory scripts
tests/testthat/       unit tests
```
